# Local Checkouts Bootstrap

XTRM runs from local git checkouts on the operator's machines, not from the npm
registry. Four repositories supply the binaries:

| Checkout | Packages linked globally | Binary |
|---|---|---|
| `core` | `xtrm-tools`, `@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions` | `xt`, `xtrm`, `ghgrep` (from committed `cli/dist`) |
| `xtrm` | `@jaggerxtrm/substrate`, `@xtrm/xtprompt`, `@xtrm/xts` | `sb`, `xtprompt`, `xts` (TypeScript run directly) |
| `xtmux` | `@jaggerxtrm/xtmux` plus `install.sh` | `xtmux`, `tmux-session-picker`, the `tmux` kill guard |
| `specialists` | `@jaggerxtrm/specialists` | `specialists`, `sp` (from committed `dist`) |

One surface installs and updates all four, per the XTRM build order: every
component is installed by `xt init`, updated by `xt update`, and checked by
`xt doctor`, from one manifest. There is no second tool and no `xt install`
command: the root command surface is guarded by `cli/test/install-surface.test.ts`.

## Where it lives

One surface installs and updates all four checkouts, per the XTRM build order.

| Surface | File | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `xt init --from-checkouts` | `cli/src/commands/init.ts` | First install: machine bootstrap, then clone/fast-forward, install and link the checkouts |
| `xt update --from-checkouts` | `cli/src/commands/update.ts` | Routine refresh: the same phase, with the built-in defaults when the machine has no configuration |
| `xt update` | same | Applies the phase on `--apply`, reports it read-only otherwise; silent on a machine with no configuration |
| `xt doctor` | `cli/src/commands/doctor.ts` | Reports the phase read-only in its own section; fails only with `--check-drift` |
| `scripts/bootstrap.sh` | repository script | Entry point for a machine that has no `xt` yet: clones `core`, then runs `xt update --from-checkouts` |

The phase itself is `cli/src/core/checkout-bootstrap.ts`; it has no dependencies
outside Node and git.

## Configuration

A machine opts in with a configuration file at `~/.xtrm/config/checkouts.json`.

```json
{
  "root": "~/dev",
  "repos": {
    "core": { "dir": "~/dev/core" }
  }
}
```

- `root` — directory that holds the sibling checkouts. Required.
- `repos.<name>` — optional per-repository override of `dir`, `remote`, `links`,
  `installer`, `extraBins`.
- `enabled: false` — keep the configuration but skip the phase.

Without this file the phase is off: `xt update` never touches links, and
`xt doctor` prints no checkout section. `xt update --from-checkouts` (or
`xt init --from-checkouts`) runs it once with the built-in defaults (`~/dev`,
the four remotes) and changes nothing in the configuration.

The `core` entry defaults to the running project's **main worktree** when that
project is the core checkout, so a run from `.xtrm/worktrees/<name>/` never
treats the worktree as the checkout. From anywhere else — `~/dev`, or a foreign
repository — `core` resolves to `<root>/core`, and the phase never installs or
links the repository the run happens to stand in.

## Usage

Run the check form first on a machine you have not updated recently, then the apply form.

```bash
xt update --from-checkouts            # clone/fast-forward, install, link, install the guard, report
xt update                             # routine refresh; reports checkouts read-only when configured
xt update --apply                     # routine refresh; applies the checkout phase too
xt init --from-checkouts              # first install on a new machine
xt doctor                             # diagnosis; checkouts section, read-only
```

Flags:

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--from-checkouts` | Run the phase even when no `checkouts.json` exists, and apply it |
| `--apply` (`xt update`) | Apply the phase on a configured machine; without it the phase reports only |
| `--json` | Machine-readable report (the `checkouts` key of the update payload) |
| `--fetch` | Refresh the remote refs before comparing; a report does not fetch by default |
| `--dry-run` (`xt init`) | Preview: the checkout phase runs in check mode and applies nothing |

Environment: `XTRM_BOOTSTRAP_NPM` selects the npm binary, `XTRM_BOOTSTRAP_ROOT`
and `XTRM_BOOTSTRAP_CORE_REMOTE` configure the `scripts/bootstrap.sh` shim.
`XTRM_BOOTSTRAP_HOME_OVERRIDE` rehearses an apply against another home (npm
prefix, `~/.local/bin`, installer state, Pi settings); the tests use it.

## Report

```
checkouts (read-only, no fetch)
  repo         branch  commit   state
  core         main    5bc81a8d ok
  xtrm         main    791a64d1 ok (untracked 3)
  xtmux        main    c8a74384 behind
  specialists  master  c17901a9 ok

  binary               resolves to                                  commit   state
  xt                   ~/dev/core/cli/dist/index.cjs                5bc81a8d ok
  sb                   ~/dev/xtrm/packages/substrate/cli/sb-ux.ts   791a64d1 ok
  tmux                 ~/dev/xtmux/bin/tmux-guard                   c8a74384 ok

drift (2)
  - xtmux: 1 commit(s) behind origin/main
  - xtmux: ~/.pi/agent/settings.json loads xtmux from the checkout directly (1 entry); the installer would add a second grouped entry

drift found: 2 finding(s), 0 problem(s); run xt update --from-checkouts to update
remote refs are the last fetched state; pass --fetch to compare with origin
```

The report names, for every linked binary, the checkout, the commit and the
package version it resolves to, plus the first entry on `PATH` when that
differs. Every line of the report — a credentialed remote, an installer
diagnostic, a problem — is redacted: URL userinfo and token-shaped strings are
removed and long text is capped before it is printed or serialised.

## Safety rules

- Uncommitted work is never discarded: no `git reset`, no `git clean`, no
  force-pull. A dirty, diverged, ahead, detached or wrong-branch checkout stops
  that repository and is reported.
- Untracked files are reported and never touched.
- A package manager may rewrite a tracked lockfile when the committed one is out
  of sync; the phase restores that file and reports `lockfile-rewritten`, so an
  update never leaves the checkout dirty.
- An installer refusal (for example xtmux declining to overwrite a
  user-customised `~/.tmux/scripts/git-pane-status.sh`) is reported with its own
  diagnostic and never forced.
- Git configuration is read, never written. A checkout wired to the retired
  Beads hooks is reported as `beads-hooks`; the fix is a manual
  `git config --unset core.hooksPath` in that checkout.
- No `tmux kill-server`, no restart of running agents. The `tmux` kill guard is
  installed by xtmux's own installer, not by this phase.
- A report run (`xt update` without `--apply`, `xt doctor`) writes nothing and
  does not fetch: it compares against the remote refs from the last fetch, so a
  commit pushed since then is not seen. `--fetch` opts into the network, which
  writes objects and remote refs, and never moves a branch.
- A report never contacts the remote to learn the default branch either: it
  reads `origin/HEAD`, the configured refspec and the tracking branches that
  already exist. Every child process has a deadline, so an unreachable or 404
  origin cannot hang the phase.

## A new machine

```bash
mkdir -p ~/dev && cd ~/dev
git clone git@github.com:xtrm-dev/core.git core
~/dev/core/scripts/bootstrap.sh
```

The shim needs `git`, Node 24 or later and `npm`. It clones `core` when the
machine has none, then runs `xt update --from-checkouts`, which clones or
fast-forwards the other three, installs dependencies, links the packages,
installs the tmux guard, and prints the report. Write
`~/.xtrm/config/checkouts.json` so later `xt update` runs keep the checkouts
current.

## The server over ssh

The phase is machine-local and read-only under `--check`:

```bash
ssh <server> '~/dev/core/cli/dist/index.cjs update --json'
```

Run it with the CLI that is already on the server; do not copy a build there to
inspect state. An apply run needs the lead's GO because it rewrites the server's
checkouts and links.

## Troubleshooting

Each finding names the repository and the action that resolves it; none of them requires a force.

| Finding | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `dirty` | tracked files modified or staged | commit, stash or discard in that checkout; nothing was changed |
| `diverged` / `ahead` | local commits not on the remote | rebase or push deliberately; the phase never rewrites history |
| `wrong-branch` / `detached` | checkout is not on the default branch | check out the default branch |
| `fetch-failed` | the `--fetch` refresh could not reach the remote, or timed out at 60 s | fix credentials or network; other repositories still update |
| `beads-hooks` | `core.hooksPath` points at the retired Beads hooks | `git config --unset core.hooksPath` in that checkout |
| `lockfile-rewritten` | committed lockfile out of sync with `package.json` | fix the lockfile in that repository |
| `installer-refused` | xtmux refused to overwrite a file it does not own | resolve the file by hand; nothing was forced |
| `pi-entry-conflict` | Pi settings load the xtmux checkout directly | remove the duplicate Pi entry before re-running the installer |
| `link-missing` / `link-mismatch` | a binary is not linked, or resolves to another checkout | re-run `xt update --from-checkouts` |
| `installer-missing` / `installer-version` | xtmux installer state is absent or stale | re-run the phase; it runs `install.sh` |
| `not-a-git-checkout` | the directory is not a checkout, or its `.git` cannot be resolved (an interrupted clone leaves a git directory with no HEAD) | move it aside and re-run; a broken checkout is never reported as `ok` |

## Why not `xt bootstrap` or `xt install`

`xt bootstrap` is the deprecated payload refresh, retained as an alias of
`xt update`; it does not touch checkouts. `xt install` does not exist: the root
command surface is guarded by `cli/test/install-surface.test.ts` and
`cli/test/command-migration.test.ts`, which require `xt install` to fail. The
build order puts the install story in one surface (`xt init` / `xt update` /
`xt doctor`), and this phase is that surface's local-checkout half.

## Tests

```bash
cd cli && npx vitest run src/tests/checkout-bootstrap.test.ts
```

The suite owns temporary homes and temporary git origins: no network, no real
`npm link`, no writes outside its scratch directories. It covers clean, dirty,
behind, diverged, missing, untracked, Beads-hook, lockfile, installer-refusal,
Pi-entry-conflict, redaction, the no-fetch report, a fresh directory outside
every checkout, a foreign repository, the init dry-run mode and idempotency.
